Pre-registered 2026-08-26 11:34, BEFORE any phase-loss checkpoint exists.

HYPOTHESIS
  The stock loss is written in ABSOLUTE frames, so its geometry changes with
  tempo and one scalar pos_weight must serve every tempo. A phase-dependent
  negative weight is tempo-invariant by construction and makes double-tempo cost
  what half-tempo costs.

    c(phi) = 1 + gamma * exp(-d(phi,1/2)^2 / (2 sigma^2)),  sigma = 0.06
    gamma = 1.3 from cost parity: 7N(1+gamma) = 16N

  Verified in unit tests: doubled-prediction loss ratio 1.72 vs halved 1.94
  (was 0.85 vs 1.94); halved untouched (ratio 1.000); gamma=0 reproduces the
  stock loss to 6 decimals; c identical at 40 and 180 bpm.

BASELINE (already measured, same corpus / seed / schedule)
  f0_shipped_s0, 100 epochs, stock loss, seed 0:
    F(217) 0.5919   doubled(<55) 0.511   halved(>100) 0.316   correct-lvl 0.576

ARMS
  fold 0, seed 0, 100 epochs, val_frequency 5 (20 checkpoints -> trajectory
  comparable against f0_shipped_s0). ONLY --loss and --phase-gamma differ from
  the baseline command; every other flag is at its stock default.
    gamma = 1.3   cost parity
    gamma = 3.0   beyond parity

PRIMARY READOUT -- the failure mode, per track, not the mean
  The mean hid the effect once already: dw32 looked flat at +0.0058 while the
  transition table showed doubled->correct flips were worth +0.0428 each,
  cancelled by an equal number of correct->halved breaks. So:

    doubled(<55) and halved(>100), intersected track sets
    the doubled->correct / correct->halved transition table vs baseline
    F(217) reported alongside, NOT as the gate

CONFIRMED  doubled falls >= 0.10 AND halved rises < 0.05 AND F does not fall
KILL       doubled falls < 0.05, OR halved rises >= 0.10 (it traded, like every
           previous knob), OR F falls >= 0.02
AMBIGUOUS  otherwise -> add seeds 1,2 before interpreting

MECHANISM CHECK (reported, does not override the rule)
  A halved prediction has no mass at phi=0.5, so c(phi) should leave halving
  ALONE. If halving moves as much as doubling, the term is acting as a generic
  rate knob like everything before it, and the phase formulation bought nothing.

WHAT THIS CANNOT CLAIM
  Absolute performance -- trains on ~43% of upstream's corpus. Measures a DELTA
  against f0_shipped_s0 only.
  The oracle screen (+0.030 SMC, +0.025 GTZAN) used GROUND-TRUTH phase and is an
  upper bound; a trained model suppresses subdivisions of its OWN inferred grid,
  which on a doubled track is the wrong grid. That gap is exactly what this run
  tests and the screen could not.
